summary: Somerset County, Maine, summit lookout from about 1905; steel tower by 1917; vacant from about 1972 and burned on site by the state on 15 April 2011.

facts.design: Steel tower with a cabin on top; a 12-by-12-foot stone foundation was built about 1960 to carry the cabin
facts.status_note: Burned on site in April 2011; no source describes the summit since.

events.note: Summit observatory; a September 1905 item calls it the third observatory on the mountain. The 2011 Sun Journal account dates the first tower to about 1905.
Station reported 11 fires in 1905, per a 1907 item
Steel tower 38 feet high, per a 1917 report; a 1920 inventory lists a 16-foot steel tower
Tower wrecked a few years before December 1925; the only earlier tower to blow over, per the Mount Abram article. The exact date is not given.
Duluth Wing says he was the watchman in the tower in 1947
Aubrey Bishop, 40, fire warden at the lookout tower, died of a heart attack in July 1949
12-by-12-foot stone foundation and livable cabin built about 1960, per Wing
May 1962 item: nine tons of material for a new fire tower airlifted to the summit
Burned on site by the state on April 15, 2011

corrections.why: Sources describe a steel fire tower (1917, 1920, a new tower in 1962) and call the 2011 burned structure a watchtower; the Association's list classes the site as Ground.

notes_for_editor: Record kind 'ground' is proposed as 'tower' (see corrections); the Association's list still says Ground, so a human should decide. Height conflict left open: 1917 says 38 ft, 1920 says 16 ft; the record's height_m 4.9 matches the 1920 figure, so height_m is not put in facts. Dates differ slightly: the cabin and foundation are dated about 1960 by Wing and a new tower airlifted in May 1962; both are given as the sources give them. Agency names vary by source (Maine Forestry District, Maine Forest Service, Maine Parks and Lands, Maine Bureau of Parks and Land). Access is not in facts: state ownership in 2011 and Appalachian Trail hiker use are reported, but no source states current public access. The FFLA 2011 report's 'Mount Blue' look-alike tower is a different site and is not used. The Facebook post and willhiteweb pages were not cited.
